• Tower/Floorstanding Speakers - Usually found in higher end home theater and dedicated 2.0 listening setups, tower speakers have several advantages AND dis-advantages over the standardbookshelf. Their larger size and internal volume mean they can be configured to reach lower in frequency than even the largest bookshelves and in most cases they can produce a far higher volume because of the number and size of the drivers being used. Choosing to use a tower comes down to budget and usage. If you plan on never buying a subwoofer, and using your setup for mostly music, you can likely go tower with no regrets. One common misconception is that towers take up more "room" than a small bookshelf but in reality the dimensions are very similar when compared to bookshelves on standard sized stands. The main problem with using a tower Vs a smaller bookshelf is ironically the low end it produces. Bass reverberates and causes waves that bounce around the room. Subwoofers are usually hard to place so having a tower get down to near subwoofer levels (<50Hz) means you may have similar problems times two and you can't do the "sub crawl" to place your towers.

  • Placement is key to get your speakers sounding right. THIS IS NOT PROPER PLACEMENT! You should allow a wide berth between your speakers and try to following some basic angular layout rules. Not all situations will accommodate what that diagram portrays but getting close to it is always going to be better than not trying at all. Moving the speakers forward and backward as little as a ¼" can affect where the vocals appear to render in space!

.

Tower Speakers------------------

.

Take Note! Towers are sold in pairs AND INDIVIDUALLY! So make sure you check carefully before buying them from anywhere. If the price seems too good to be true you may be buying just one speaker. I will fill in the price for a Pair below.

.

Price-- Item------------------ Description- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -  
$130 Dayton T652's These only just squeek into the list. While technically towers you can see in my review that these should really be treated as a simple set of GIANT BOOKSHELF SPEAKERS!  
$175 Pioneer FS-SP52 There is no other/cheaper way to break into the world of tower speakers then with these Andrew Jones Pioneers. A bit boomy and with soft highs they are more musical in nature but work amazingly for Home Theater duties. They also go for $99 or less when on sale.  
$300 BIC FT-6T When people ask what speakers for Home theater and occasional parties. These are those speakers. I have even recommended them for an aircraft hanger or two (seriously). Loud is what defines these baby bic's. If gentle and neutral are what you are after, keep looking.  
$500 Fluance XL7F Take a good look at these. Fluance loves to play with unique designs and these are no different. This tower is the only one I can find featuring a large, down-firing 8" driver to act as a dedicated Subwoofer inside of each speaker. You will be impressed by these.  
$600 BIC PL-89 II The poor mans Klipsch or more? BIC offers a similar sound signature but you can usually get a driver size larger and STILL spend less than the equivalent Klipsch. They also tout the extremely high achievable decibel levels which makes these the party speakers.  
$620 Klipsch RF-52 II The Murder Klipsch. There are also 6" and 8" variants of this reference design but for simplicity and sanity and budget sake I will let you guys search them out on your own. I don't even need to describe how these sound all you need do is look at them.  
$850 Chane A5rx-c From a small company with everything to prove the build of these monsters stinks of a vengence blood-lust against the "big brands" trying to show off what more exotic components can achieve at relatively cheap prices.  
$1100 JBL Studio 570 JBL have more engineers working round the clock on their high end and professional stuff than any audio other company (Citation Needed). These speakers certainly show what hardcore research can do to your speakers.  

.

I can't possibly encompass all the options available to you in these lists. There are so many other models and boutique sites that sell direct like Zu Audio, Aperion and NHT so figure out your speaker budget, stick firm and look at all the options.

.

  • Self-Powered Monitors - In professional applications like a recording studio, certain criteria have to be met for sound reproduction. To assure that Song A sounds like Song A when you play it back ANYWHERE the monitors most songs are mastered on have to sound very similar (search Yamaha NS-10..) They attempt to achieve a flat and un-colored frequency response and not leave too much for the end-user to "adjust". In the world of professional monitors what you get is what you get. You may have to buy some special wires or Adapters to hook them up but in terms of simplicity.. Power+Signal=Done. Some units have amps in each speaker and others just feed power from one to the other so be mindful of what connections your desk needs to support them.

  • The negatives.. If you want to upgrade powered monitors, be prepared to buy an entirely new set of monitors. Unlike Speaker+Amp setups your amplifiers are IN your speakers. If you don't like the way your monitors sound you will have to modify the source or an addon EQ most times. Also adding a subwoofer now requires a subwoofer with Line-In/Out's and forces you to control volume via pre-amp or PC and not the gain knobs of either the sub or monitors.

.

Powered Monitors------------------

.

In some cases Powered Monitors are also sold individually. If I can't find a pair bundle I will indicate in the description you need two and list the price for a pair.

.

Price-- Item------------------ Description- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -  
$100 Micca PB42x VIDEO REVIEW While not technically designed for mixing and mastering applications the renowned MB42x's with a built in amplifier is still an incredible bargain at a hundred bucks! Also a birdie tells me if you use this instead of the stock power supply, you get 50wpc  
$290 JBL LSR305 VIDEO REVIEW Sold Individually. As the highest Rated Powered Monitor on all of amazon this needs to be here. I haven't had the chance to hear these but when JBL want to impress the masses they don't have to do much. Praise and a future spot on my desk is what these have.  
$300 KRK Rockit 5 Probably the most popular of all powered monitors KRK has become known for the volume and low end their monitors produce. From PC setups to Home theater 2.0 setups I think I have seen that yellow cone everywhere. Price to Performance 12/10.  
$300 Emotiva Airmotiv4s Having a Transducer instead of a tweeter is what makes the Emotiva line of monitors stand out. This, their smallest unit, has an astonishing amount of praise from all audio forums. Their passive speakers may be gone, but these will live on.  
$400 Yamaha HS5 Known for their flat response these modern day yamaha's reflect back to the most popular monitor of the whole of the world.. The NS-10. These white cones have become synonymous with professional studio's the world over.  
$400 AudioEngine A5+ This is the default Powered monitor recommendation. They are clear, small and very well reviewed. I don't want to say they sound boring but very neutral. They don't get quite as loud as others in this category but the overall quality can not be disputed.  
$500 Vanatoo T1 I spent a good deal of time with these. And although not marketed as "Professional Studio Monitors" they are the most impressive powered monitors I have ever heard. Their Small size, connectivity and tremendous low end more than make up for the price.  

.

Be sure to google full rear images OR EVEN BETTER, download the manuals for whatever monitors you are interested in and check the rear panel connections. Some have RCA inputs so you would just need TWO lengthy individual RCA's (usually the ones designed for subwoofers work well). If TRS 1/4" is the only thing there you can get adapters or premade cables to hook them up to an RCA source. If your source is a 3.5mm output just get a 3.5mm to RCA adapter and you should be set.
